findings.source_quote: ὥρισεν πρότερον πιστεύσαντας αὐτῷ ἰωμένῳ τὰ σώματα σώζεσθαι, ἔπειτα καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἐπανορθοῦσθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀνώλεθρον
findings.english_quote: he determined that those who first believed in him as he healed the bodies would be saved, and afterward that their souls too would be restored to imperishability
findings.issue: The main rendering defensibly attaches τὰ σώματα to ἰωμένῳ as its object, but the notes omit a material alternative: τὰ σώματα can specify the bodily scope of σώζεσθαι, yielding salvation in body followed by restoration of the souls. The existing alternative, “believed him, the one healing the bodies,” changes the treatment of the participle but retains the same attachment of τὰ σώματα. It therefore does not disclose the alternative body/soul construction. This is insufficient disclosure, not an unreadable source or a reason to block the passage.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to explain that the current rendering takes τὰ σώματα as the object of the immediately preceding healing participle. Preserve the alternative: “he determined that, after first believing in him who heals, they should be saved in body, and afterward that their souls too should be restored to imperishability.” Explain that this alternative connects τὰ σώματα with σώζεσθαι and makes the parallel with τὰς ψυχὰς explicit. The revised note, and any changed main rendering, require fresh review.

findings.source_quote: δι’ ἃς . . . . οὐδὲ ζητεῖν τὸ συμφέρον οὐ διεφύλαξαν
findings.english_quote: because of those pleasures . . . . they did not even continue to seek what is beneficial
findings.issue: The draft correctly retains the printed gap, and its source issue honestly identifies the unavailable wording. Nevertheless, the missing segment prevents verification of the causal statement’s complete content. The failed coverage check concerns missing source content, not an omission of extant Greek by the translator. The block does not arise merely from the disclosed double-negative ambiguity, the unaccented του, or the intelligible spelling ἐνχειρῆσαι; none of those requires treating the verified print as an OCR error.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the printed gap and the explicit incompleteness notice; do not invent connecting words or silently restore the clause. Recovering the missing meaning would require separately identified textual evidence, not merely another inspection of the already image-checked printing. Any proposed restoration must remain clearly distinguished from the supplied Lagarde reading and undergo fresh review. Without that evidence, this passage cannot be certified as having complete recoverable content.
